newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields ignore EMU worries, end flat.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields ignore EMU worries, end flat.

text.p: Long Swedish bond yields ended flat on Thursday despite general worries in Germany and France over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), while the crown weakened in thin trade.

"One reason that made Sweden escape turmoil today was the new Riksbank rules, which increase its independence," a dealer said. "It doesn't matter so much if we end up outside EMU when we have such an independent central bank."
The crown softened but recovered somewhat after the Riksbank intervened and bought crowns for marks at around 4.54 crowns to the mark, although the unit weakened again in late trade.
When the bond market closed, the crown was changing hands at 4.5350 to mark, compared to 4.5210 on Wednesday.
Dealers attributed the crown's poor performance to thin trade and a London bank selling a lot of crowns against marks just before the intervention.
The six month T-bill rate rose two basis points to 4.32 percent while the ten year bond yield was unchanged at 7.11.
Players will watch the ruling Social Democrats executive committee meeting on Friday, hoping the party will announce its EMU view. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
